questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(\frac{\pi }{2})=⟨3,0,-4⟩,\,{q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})=⟨0,3,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5})\cdot q(t)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{5}\cdot q(t)+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{5}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{5}\cdot q(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{5}\cdot {q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{q}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{3}{5}⟨0,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{3}{5}⟨0,1,0⟩}{(\frac{3}{5})} \\  & =⟨0,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{1}{5}q(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot ⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨3,0,-4⟩\cdot ⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\cdot 0+0\cdot 1-4\cdot 0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=\sqrt{2}\,i+j+k,\,{q}^{′}(0)=-2\,j+2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2(0)}{({0}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{1}{{0}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =0(\sqrt{2}\,i+j+k)+\frac{1}{2}(-2\,j+2\,k) \\  & =-j+k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{-j+k}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-j+k)\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{2}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-j+k) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{2}\,i+j+k)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-j+k) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(-j\cdot j+k\cdot k) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(-1+1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
T(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩.
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
$⟨$
{{field-1}},

$\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =2⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =2‖⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩‖ \\  & =2\sqrt{{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =2\sqrt{1} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩}{2} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\,i+\sqrt{3}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,k).
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
$\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,i\,-$
{{field-1}}
$k$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\,i+\sqrt{3}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,k)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1))\,i+\sqrt{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1))\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\,k)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{2}‖\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\,k‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1))^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(t+1)+{sin}^{2}⁡(t+1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\,k)}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{5}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j-4\,k).
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
{{field-1}}
$i\,+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{5}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j-4\,k)) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)\,k) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{3}{5}‖\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j‖ \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{3}{5}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)}{\frac{3}{5}} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$
